report.root_cause: The 07:16 server.properties deploy (ticket OPS-250, meant only to raise max-players from 20 to 40) also set white-list=true and enforce-whitelist=true, compared with deploy/previous/server.properties where both were false. whitelist.json is an empty list, so every connection was rejected with "You are not whitelisted on this server!", including the regular players Alex_Builds and Steve_Mines, who were disconnected at 07:17.
report.actions: Checked status and logs; saw repeated "not whitelisted" disconnects starting at 07:17. Read server.properties, whitelist.json (empty), deploy/2026-11-01-server-properties.md, and deploy/previous/server.properties, and diffed them. Declared the incident. Ran console command "whitelist off" at runtime (confirmed "Whitelist is now turned off"), so players could rejoin without a restart. Rewrote server.properties with enforce-whitelist=false and white-list=false, keeping the approved max-players=40 and all other values unchanged. Did not restart the server. Verified from the logs that whitelist rejections stopped after 07:17:45, and that Alex_Builds and Steve_Mines were back online. TPS stayed at 20 and MSPT stayed low throughout.
report.residual_risk: The runtime whitelist change is only in memory until the file takes effect; the file now says white-list=false, so a restart will match. whitelist.json is still empty and was not restored, since its previous contents are unknown and whitelisting was not in the previous config. online-mode=false (offline mode) was already set in the previous config and was left unchanged, but it lets anyone connect with any username and needs a separate review. Brief newplayer22-26 join/leave pairs at 07:18 are unexplained probe-like connections and were not investigated further. The deploy process should be checked so that config diffs beyond the ticket's scope are caught.
